revision_responses.344-2:
RESEARCH QUESTIONS

RQ1. When LLM participants who first answer in isolation are then exposed
to the declared positions of their peers, how often do they change
position without declaring new grounds?

RQ2. What is the effective sample size of the panel before and after that
exposure, and how much of the nominal panel size is lost to dependence
between participants?

HYPOTHESES

H1 (peer exposure). The rate of position change without newly declared
grounds is higher in the exposed condition (E), in which a participant
sees the prior contributions of all participants, than in the
self-anchoring condition (B3), in which it sees only its own prior
contribution.

    Delta_herd = rate(E) - rate(B3) > 0

H2 (self-anchoring). The rate of position change under exposure to one's
own prior answer differs from the rate under blind repetition.

    Delta_self = rate(B3) - rate(B2)

This quantity is reported as a result in its own right. It is the
quantity that studies comparing round 1 with round N attribute to peer
exposure, and it is confounded with it whenever B3 is absent.

H3 (effective sample size). For any mean dependence in (0, 1], the
effective sample size of a panel of n participants, computed through the
design effect

    N_eff = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho_bar)

is substantially below n. The primary quantity of this study is the
difference between conditions:

    Delta_N_eff = N_eff(B1) - N_eff(E)

that is, the cost of exposure expressed in effective observations.
rho_bar is estimated as the mean pairwise correlation between binary
error vectors on the subset of items with ground truth.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED

This study does not claim that convergence is an error, that a
participant which changes position performs worse, that disagreement
implies independence, or that the observed dependence is caused by
conformity rather than by shared pre-training data. The discount on
N_eff holds under either mechanism, and the design does not separate
them.

revision_responses.344-14:
The experiment is executed on Norvald Studio, an open multi-LLM
deliberation platform developed by the author, which is used here solely
as the instrument.

Pilot runs are used only to calibrate item difficulty into a usable
disagreement range. The question bank is frozen by fingerprint before the
main round, and no item is edited afterwards. Pilot responses are not
part of the analysed data.

Randomised presentation order of peer contributions is recorded per
execution, so position effects remain analysable rather than assumed away.
344-17: Randomized Experiment: Must include random assignment of subjects to treatments or conditions. This usually includes lab experiments, field experiments, intervention experiments, randomized controlled trials, and A/B testing.
344-27: Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.
344-32: Subjects will not be aware of the assigned treatment during data collection (either because the subjects are not human participants or because of blinding procedures).
revision_responses.344-38:
The outcome requires no coding judgement. Each participant declares a
discrete, pre-specified option through a machine-readable relation
(decision --selects--> option), so the measured position is read
mechanically rather than interpreted by a coder. There is no rater to
blind, and no semantic judge anywhere in the measurement path.

Change of position and the presence or absence of newly declared grounds
are derived deterministically from the recorded structure, by rules fixed
before the main round.
revision_responses.344-40:
Fully within-subject (repeated measures). Every participant is observed
under every condition; there is no assignment of participants to groups.

PARTICIPANTS. Four LLMs from four distinct families, held within the same
size class to avoid confounding dependence with capability. A homogeneous
contrast panel of four instances of a single model is run under B1 only.

TASK. 44 self-contained multiple-choice items with 2 to 4 mutually
exclusive, pre-declared options: 32 contestable items and a subset of 12
binary items with verifiable ground truth. Options are seeded into the
Working Context as `option` items before the first wave. Each participant
declares `decision --selects--> option`.

CONDITIONS. Four, differing in what is present in the Working Context at
execution time:

    B1  first answer, blind. Fresh session. Sees neither peers nor any
        prior answer of its own.
    B2  blind repetition of B1. Fresh session, same task and
        configuration. Estimates spontaneous instability.
    B3  second wave over B1, with only its own first-wave contribution
        present. Estimates self-anchoring.
    E   second wave over B1, with the contributions of all participants
        present. Peer exposure.

B1 and B2 are independent executions. B3 and E are second-wave executions
over the same first wave and are therefore necessarily posterior.

CRITICAL FEATURE OF THE EXPOSED CONDITION. Exposure is simultaneous, not
sequential. In the second wave every participant sees the same complete
set of first-wave contributions, and no participant sees any second-wave
answer of any other. Dependence is therefore induced by a common cause —
the shared first-wave Working Context — rather than by ordered contagion
between respondents. This preserves the exchangeability assumed by the
design-effect estimator, which sequential debate would violate.

EXECUTION VOLUME. 16 executions per item for the main panel (704 across
44 items), plus 4 per item for the contrast panel (176 in B1).

ORDER AND DRIFT. B1 and B2 are interleaved item by item rather than run
as blocks, so that provider drift affects both equally and cancels in the
difference instead of being confounded with condition. B3 and E are
likewise interleaved with each other.

OUTCOMES.
    Delta_self  = rate(B3) - rate(B2)
    Delta_herd  = rate(E)  - rate(B3)
    N_eff       = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho_bar), per condition
    Delta_N_eff = N_eff(B1) - N_eff(E)

rho_bar is estimated as the mean pairwise correlation between binary
error vectors, computed on the 12-item ground-truth subset. Agreement on
the contestable subset is reported separately as a descriptive quantity
and does not feed the effective-sample-size table.

EXCLUSION, DECLARED IN ADVANCE. An item on which all four participants
agree in B1 does not enter the main analysis: there is no variation to
observe. The discard rate is reported as a result. A minimum of 20
surviving contestable items is required; if piloting projects fewer, the
bank is expanded before the main round, never after it begins.

The full protocol, including threats to validity and the frozen
configuration, is attached as 01_Protocolo_Experimental.md.
revision_responses.344-44:
Two randomisations, both at the level of a single execution.

1. Presentation order of peer contributions within the exposed condition.
The order in which the first-wave contributions appear in the prompt is
drawn independently for each execution, and the drawn order is recorded
with that execution. Recording matters: an unrecorded randomisation
cannot be analysed afterwards, only assumed to have cancelled out, so
position effects remain testable rather than presumed neutral.

2. Interleaving of conditions across items. B1 and B2 alternate item by
item rather than being run as separate blocks, and B3 and E likewise, so
that drift in hosted models is distributed evenly across conditions
instead of aligning with them.

No randomisation of participants to conditions is performed or required:
the design is fully within-subject and every participant is observed
under every condition.
revision_responses.344-47:
POPULATION AND SAMPLING FRAME. The units are not people. Two units of
analysis are nested: the participant (an LLM under a frozen
configuration) and the item (a multiple-choice question).

PARTICIPANT SELECTION. Four models from four distinct model families,
selected within a single size class. Holding capability roughly constant
is deliberate: diversity metrics in LLM ensembles are strongly entangled
with capability, so a panel mixing size classes would measure capability
while appearing to measure dependence. A homogeneous contrast panel of
four instances of one model is run under B1 only, as the reference point
for maximal dependence.

FROZEN CONFIGURATION. Provider, model identifier, version snapshot,
temperature, top_p and maximum tokens are fixed and recorded before the
main round and are not altered during it. Every execution stores the
resolved configuration, so drift in a hosted model is detectable after
the fact rather than silently absorbed.

ITEM CONSTRUCTION. 44 self-contained items, each carrying all necessary
context in its statement, with 2 to 4 mutually exclusive pre-declared
options. Two subsets: 32 contestable items, and 12 binary items with
verifiable ground truth. Every ground-truth key is verified before any
execution, since a wrong key inverts the error signal on that item and
contaminates the dependence estimate without producing any visible
anomaly in the analysis.

INCLUSION AND EXCLUSION, DECLARED IN ADVANCE. An item on which all four
participants select the same option in B1 is excluded from the main
analysis: with no variation there is nothing to observe. The discard
rate is itself reported as a result, not treated as loss.

ACKNOWLEDGED LIMITATION. The item bank is written by the author, who is
also testing the hypothesis, and statements are adjusted after piloting
until blind disagreement falls in a usable range. This is legitimate
calibration and is declared as such. It is bounded by freezing the bank
by fingerprint before the main round, after which no statement, option
or key is edited.

COLLECTION. Executions are issued through hosted provider APIs. Each
takes roughly 3 to 15 seconds; the binding constraint is requests per
minute, not compute. Expected duration of the main round is on the order
of hours, not days. Every execution persists its prompt, raw response,
declared structure, resolved configuration and timestamp.

Full detail, including the item bank and the threat table, is in the
attached 01_Protocolo_Experimental.md.
revision_responses.344-51:
Two nested levels.

PARTICIPANTS
    main panel        4 models, 4 distinct families, one size class
    contrast panel    4 instances of a single model, B1 only

ITEMS
    contestable       32
    ground truth      12 (binary)
    total             44

EXECUTIONS
    main panel     16 per item  (4 participants x 4 conditions)
                   44 items  ->  704 executions
    contrast panel  4 per item in B1 only
                   44 items  ->  176 executions
    pilots          48 (ground-truth difficulty) + 20 (disagreement, 5 items)

Sample size is identical across conditions by construction: every
participant is observed under every condition on every item.

The n of the primary test is not 44. The main test is McNemar over
discordant pairs, so the effective n is the number of surviving
contestable items after the exclusion rule, with a pre-specified floor of
20. The effective-sample-size table rests on the 12-item ground-truth
subset and on no other part of the bank.
revision_responses.344-53:
Not a power analysis. The binding constraints are declared floors rather
than a target effect size, because no prior estimate of the effect of
peer exposure on effective sample size exists to power against — the
nearest precedent measures panels whose members never interact.

Three pre-specified floors:

    20 surviving contestable items, because the n of the McNemar test is
    the number of survivors, not the number of items written. If piloting
    projects fewer, the bank is expanded before the main round.

    8 ground-truth items producing at least one error, because below that
    the co-failure ratio has no empirical anchor and the analytic half of
    the study degenerates into algebra.

    4 participants, set by the requirement to hold capability constant
    across four distinct families rather than by statistical power.

Cost is not a constraint: the full design is on the order of two dollars
with hosted providers.
revision_responses.344-55:
PILOTING ENDS, AND COLLECTION BEGINS, AT A SINGLE EVENT: the fingerprint
of the item bank is recorded. From that point no statement, option or key
is edited. Two pilots must pass first.

Pilot 1 — ground-truth difficulty. 12 items x 4 participants in B1, 48
calls.
    all four correct   -> item too easy, replaced from reserve
    all four wrong     -> verify the key before accepting the item
    disagreement whose stated justifications reveal different readings
                       -> ambiguous statement, rewritten or replaced
If fewer than 8 items still produce error after replacement, new items
are written before proceeding.

Pilot 2 — disagreement calibration. Five items spanning 2, 3 and 4
options. If blind disagreement does not fall between 30% and 70%,
statements are adjusted before the rest of the budget is spent. If the
pilot projects fewer than 20 surviving contestable items, the bank is
expanded before the main round rather than after it starts.

STOPPING. Collection terminates when the planned matrix is complete: 704
main-panel executions and 176 contrast-panel executions. There is no
data-dependent stopping. The number of executions is fixed in advance and
is not revised in response to interim results, so no optional-stopping
bias can enter the dependence estimate.

Executions that fail for transport or provider reasons are retried under
the identical frozen configuration and both attempts are recorded. A
failed execution is never silently replaced by a fresh draw.
revision_responses.344-58:
One factor, four levels, fully within-subject. Every participant is
observed at every level on every item.

FACTOR: content of the Working Context at execution.

  B1  empty of specialist knowledge.
  B2  identical to B1; a second independent draw.
  B3  its own first-wave contribution only.
  E   first-wave contributions of all participants.

One element added per step: B1 to B2 adds nothing (spontaneous
instability); B2 to B3 adds its own prior answer (self-anchoring);
B3 to E adds the peers (exposure).

Held fixed: items, options, provider, version, sampling parameters.
revision_responses.344-62:
PRIMARY OUTCOME, PER EXECUTION

 selected_option  the option declared via the relation
   decision--selects-->option. Categorical, 2 to 4 pre-declared
   levels. Read mechanically; no coder, no semantic judge.

DERIVED PER PARTICIPANT AND ITEM

 changed_position  second-wave option differs from own B1 option.
 new_grounds  declares a ground absent from its own B1 contribution.
   Strict reading: a ground targeting another participant does NOT
   count as new. A permissive reading is reported alongside, as an
   interval.
 error  ground-truth subset only.
 confidence  as declared; absence never coerced to zero.

ALSO RECORDED

 participant, model, provider, version, condition, item, wave,
 timestamp, sampling parameters, drawn order of peer contributions,
 raw response, parsed structure, parser rejection.

SUBSETTING

 all_agree_B1  item excluded from the main analysis.
 seeded  a participant absent from the Working Context was seen by
   nobody.
revision_responses.344-66:
1. RATE, per condition c in {B2,B3,E}

 rate(c) = changed_position AND NOT new_grounds, over valid
 participant-item pairs in c

2. DECOMPOSITION

 Delta_self = rate(B3) - rate(B2)   own prior answer
 Delta_herd = rate(E)  - rate(B3)   the peers, isolated

3. DEPENDENCE, ground-truth items only

 Per participant, a binary error vector over those items. For each
 of the 6 pairs, the phi between their error vectors.

 rho_bar = mean of the 6 pairwise phi values

 Error vectors, not agreement over selections: kappa equals the
 intraclass correlation the design effect needs only in the binary
 case with exchangeable raters.

4. EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE, per condition, n = 4

 N_eff = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho_bar)

5. PRIMARY QUANTITY

 Delta_N_eff = N_eff(B1) - N_eff(E)

 rho_bar in E carries shared origin plus exposure, B1 only the
 first, so the difference isolates exposure.

6. SWEEP

 N_eff over rho_bar in (0,1] and n in {4,8,inf}. Analytic; the
 observed value is an anchor, not a bound.
revision_responses.344-71:
Paired design throughout: the same participant, on the same item, across
conditions. No model is fitted across independent groups.

H1 — PEER EXPOSURE, PARTICIPANT LEVEL
    Test      McNemar on discordant pairs, proportion of position change
              without newly declared grounds, E against B3.
    Unit      participant x item.
    Effect    difference of proportions with a bootstrap confidence
              interval.

H2 — SELF-ANCHORING, PARTICIPANT LEVEL
    Test      the same McNemar, B3 against B2. Estimates Delta_self.
    Reported as a result in its own right, not only as a control.

ASYMMETRY, BY MODEL PAIR
    The same conditional rate computed per ordered model pair, to detect
    who pulls and who is pulled. Descriptive; no inferential claim is
    attached to individual pairs.

PANEL LEVEL
    McNemar answers whether an individual conforms. Effective sample size
    is a property of the panel, and the two are linked but not identical:
    a panel can converge without any single participant changing more
    than noise would predict.

    Test      paired Wilcoxon on the per-item dispersion change,
              E against B3.
    Unit      the item. This puts n in the tens rather than at the count
              of discordant cells, which is the power constraint of the
              participant-level test.

CONFIDENCE CHANNEL
    Test      paired Wilcoxon on the change in declared confidence,
              E against B3.
    Conditioned on whether the majority of peers agrees or disagrees with
    the participant's own position. Confidence conformity predicts a rise
    in the first case and a fall in the second; that asymmetry is more
    informative than the mean and is the form in which it is reported.

DEPENDENCE AND EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE
    Not a hypothesis test. rho_bar_error is estimated as the mean
    pairwise phi between binary error vectors on the 12 ground-truth
    items, and N_eff = n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho_bar) is evaluated per
    condition, with n = 4.

    With four participants and twelve binary items, N_eff is a point
    estimate with wide uncertainty. It is reported with a bootstrap
    interval over items and is never presented as a precise figure.

    For this reason the sensitivity sweep is the primary analytic
    artefact: N_eff over the full range of rho_bar in (0, 1] and over
    n in {4, 8, infinity}. That table is analytic, holds regardless of
    the value estimated here, and is labelled as analytic rather than
    empirical. The observed rho_bar_error enters it as an empirical
    anchor, not as a bound.

ASSUMPTION CHECK THAT GATES THE ESTIMATOR
    The design effect assumes exchangeable units with a common rho. This
    holds here because exposure is simultaneous: in the second wave every
    participant sees the same complete set of first-wave contributions
    and none sees another's second-wave answer, so dependence is induced
    by a common cause rather than by ordered contagion. Sequential debate
    would violate the assumption and the estimator would not be reported.
    If the execution log shows that any participant's second-wave input
    contained another participant's second-wave output, the affected
    items are excluded from the N_eff table and the exclusion is
    reported.

POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    Negative control   B2, blind repetition. Any change here is
                       spontaneous instability, and Delta_self and
                       Delta_herd are both measured against it.
    Positive control   the homogeneous panel in B1, four instances of a
                       single model, as the reference point for maximal
                       dependence.

POWER
    No power analysis precedes piloting, because no prior estimate of the
    effect of exposure on N_eff exists to power against. A rough effect
    estimate is computed from a pilot of 5 to 8 items and reported; the
    paired design is substantially more efficient than an independent
    one, and n is not fixed against an invented effect size.
revision_responses.344-75:
No numerical transformation, centering or rescaling is performed.

CODING
    selected_option     categorical, kept as the declared option
                        identifier. Never mapped onto an ordinal or
                        numeric scale: the options are mutually
                        exclusive and unordered.
    changed_position    0/1
    new_grounds         0/1, under two readings reported as an interval:
                        strict, in which a ground whose target belongs to
                        another participant's contribution does not count
                        as new; and permissive, in which it does.
    error               0/1, ground-truth subset only.
    confidence          used as declared. Absence is recorded as absent
                        and excluded pairwise; it is never coerced to
                        zero, because an undeclared confidence is not a
                        confidence of zero.

AGREEMENT METRIC
    Fleiss kappa over the four participants, per item, aggregated over
    the set. Pairwise kappa is used only in the asymmetry analysis.

    Two dependence estimators are reported and are not interchangeable:

        rho_bar_behaviour   agreement beyond chance, contestable subset
        rho_bar_error       co-failure beyond chance, ground-truth subset

    Only rho_bar_error feeds the N_eff table. Kappa coincides with the
    intraclass correlation the design effect requires only in the binary
    case with exchangeable raters; with three or four options and unequal
    marginals the two diverge and the substitution is not valid.
    rho_bar_behaviour is reported as a descriptive quantity, outside the
    table.

    The distance between the two estimators is itself reported: it
    measures how much the absence of ground truth distorts the estimate,
    which is the situation of nearly every real panel deployment.

DECLARED RETRACTION
    An earlier version of this protocol derived a lower bound on rho_bar
    from observed agreement. That inference does not hold: agreement
    above chance includes agreement produced by easy items, where
    participants agree for good reason. Observed behavioural agreement is
    therefore a candidate ceiling, not a floor. No floor is assumed, and
    the sensitivity sweep covers the full range.
revision_responses.344-77:
Alpha 0.05. Two-tailed throughout, including for H1, despite the
directional hypothesis: a change in the opposite direction would be a
finding and must remain detectable rather than be defined away.

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS
    Three confirmatory tests are declared in advance:
        1. McNemar, E vs B3          (Delta_herd)
        2. McNemar, B3 vs B2         (Delta_self)
        3. Wilcoxon, dispersion, E vs B3
    Holm-Bonferroni across these three. Reported both uncorrected and
    corrected, so the effect of the correction is visible.

    The confidence-channel test and the per-pair asymmetry analysis are
    exploratory. They are reported with uncorrected p-values and are
    explicitly labelled exploratory; no confirmatory claim rests on them.

EFFECT SIZES
    Every test is reported with an effect size and a bootstrap confidence
    interval. A significant result with a negligible difference of
    proportions is reported as such.

N_eff
    No significance test is attached to N_eff. It is a derived quantity,
    reported as a point estimate with a bootstrap interval alongside the
    full sensitivity sweep.

INTERPRETING A NULL RESULT
    A null Delta_herd is not a failure of the study. Delta_self large
    with Delta_herd null would mean that literature comparing round 1
    with round N has been attributing to peer exposure an effect that is
    self-anchoring. That outcome is reported as a finding, and the
    reporting is not conditional on the direction of the result.
revision_responses.344-79:
DECLARED BEFORE ANY EXECUTION

    1. Item on which all four participants select the same option in B1
       is excluded from the main analysis: no variation, nothing to
       observe. The discard rate is reported as a result.

    2. Participant whose first-wave response declared no structured
       contribution does not enter the Working Context and therefore was
       not seen by anyone. Such a participant is excluded from the
       exposure analysis for that item, and the exclusion is recorded
       per item, because a participant nobody saw cannot have induced
       conformity in others.

    3. Ground-truth item whose key fails verification is removed before
       any execution, not after seeing results.

    4. Execution that fails for transport or provider reasons is retried
       under the identical frozen configuration. Both attempts are
       recorded and the retry is used. A failed execution is never
       silently replaced by a fresh draw.

OUTLIERS
    No outlier rule. The primary outcomes are binary at the
    participant-item level; there is no continuous quantity in which a
    single observation could be extreme. Declared confidence is ordinal
    and analysed by rank, which bounds the influence of extreme values
    without discarding them.

NO OTHER EXCLUSION
    No item, participant or execution is excluded for any reason arising
    after the results are seen.
revision_responses.344-81:
Missingness is expected in two forms, and each is handled by a rule
fixed in advance rather than imputed.

    1. Undeclared confidence. Analysed pairwise: the confidence tests use
       only participant-item pairs where confidence is declared in both
       conditions being compared. Absence is never coerced to zero.

    2. Contribution rejected by the parser, or a response with no
       declared structured block. Recorded as such and excluded from the
       analyses that depend on declared structure. The rejection rate is
       reported per condition, because a rate that differs across
       conditions would itself be an effect of the manipulation rather
       than noise.

No imputation is performed. No model substitutes a value for a missing
observation. All analyses run on available data, and the amount and
distribution of missingness is reported alongside every result that it
touches.
revision_responses.344-83:
Secondary and exploratory, declared here so that they are not mistaken
for confirmatory findings later.

    1. Distance between rho_bar_behaviour and rho_bar_error. How much the
       absence of ground truth distorts a dependence estimate. Relevant
       because nearly every real panel deployment has no ground truth.

    2. Homogeneous contrast panel. rho_bar and N_eff for four instances
       of a single model in B1, as the reference point for maximal
       dependence.

    3. Pairwise asymmetry. Conditional change rates by ordered model
       pair, to see whether influence is directional.

    4. Position effects. The drawn presentation order of peer
       contributions is recorded per execution, so whether a
       contribution's position in the prompt predicts conformity is
       testable rather than assumed neutral.

    5. Literal collision between participants. The rate at which two
       participants emit a byte-identical declared claim in the blind
       wave, recorded as an author pair and a count per wave, never as
       the text of the claim. This is the cheapest possible observable of
       content redundancy: deterministic, requiring no embedding and no
       semantic judge. It serves as the surface-artefact baseline that
       any structural measure of reasoning would have to outperform.

    6. Normalisation audit. Per blind wave, the number of distinct
       declared positions in the raw contributions compared with the
       number surviving in the Working Context. A merge is legitimate
       when the merged units declared the same option and destructive
       when they declared different ones. Deterministic count, no
       judgement. A non-zero destructive rate would mean the
       deliberation framework reduces divergence before any participant
       deliberates, which would be an effect of the instrument on the
       measured quantity and is reported as such.
revision_responses.344-86:
RELATION TO THE NEAREST PRIOR WORK

Kohli (2026), "Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors
Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels" (arXiv:2605.29800), applies the Kish
effective sample size to a panel of nine LLMs from seven families on an
NLI task, estimating dependence as the mean pairwise phi between binary
error vectors, and reports that the panel supplies roughly 2.18
independent votes. It also reports n_eff per condition for prompt
variants, label ordering, temperature (1.94 to 2.18) and chain-of-thought
(phi = 0.456, n_eff = 1.94).

That work is the direct precedent, and this registration records that it
was known and read before any data for the present study existed.

Consequently, this study does not claim to introduce effective sample
size to LLM panels, nor to be the first to characterise it under
sampling temperature or under chain-of-thought reasoning. Those claims
are Kohli's.

The nine judges in that work never see one another: temperature 0.0,
standardised prompt, no communication and no iterative refinement. Its
n_eff is therefore a static property of a panel that does not interact.

The present study measures a different object: what peer exposure does to
that property. Kohli establishes the floor in isolated panels; this study
measures what exposure does to that floor. The framing is deliberately
narrower, not broader — isolated panels are the dominant case in practice
(self-consistency, best-of-n, LLM-as-a-judge, ensembles), and exposure is
a subset of that practice.

A line-by-line comparison with Kohli, including what this study can no
longer claim, is attached as 04_Confronto_com_Kohli_2026.md.

Hao et al. (2026), arXiv:2606.00820, decompose stance convergence in
multi-agent debate into spontaneous instability, conformity and
persuasion through controlled counterfactual conditions. Decomposing
conformity is therefore not novel either. What remains open is the
intersection: conformity expressed as a loss of effective sample size.
Kohli has the estimator and no exposure; Hao has exposure and no
estimator.

SCOPE OF THE EXPOSURE TREATMENT

The stimulus in the exposed condition is not "each participant saw the
others' prose". It is a single structured document that every participant
saw identically: a Working Context holding the first-wave contributions,
normalised by the same parser used in production.

This raises internal validity and reproducibility — replicating a
free-prose debate study requires reproducing whatever text the models
emitted, whereas replicating this requires reproducing a Working Context
— and narrows external validity. Delta_herd measured here is exposure to
a structured collective artefact, and a figure obtained under it is not
directly comparable to one obtained in free-prose debate. This is
declared rather than left implicit.

A registered but untested hypothesis follows from it: the Working Context
delivers declared positions without the prose that supports them, and a
bare conclusion may be easier to copy than an argument is to refute. If
so, part of Delta_herd is an effect of format rather than of the peer. A
raw-prose arm over the same first wave would separate the two and would
restore comparability with the literature. It is not part of this
registration.

INSTRUMENT AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST

The experiment runs on Norvald Studio, an open multi-LLM deliberation
platform developed by the author, used here solely as the instrument. The
author has an interest in the platform. This is disclosed because the
platform is also the object of the scope limitation described above: a
result showing that structured deliberation costs effective sample size
would not be favourable to the instrument, and the analysis plan is fixed
here precisely so that the direction of the result cannot be chosen
afterwards.

INDEPENDENT RESEARCH

The author holds no institutional affiliation and no funding. The study
is self-funded and costs on the order of two dollars in hosted provider
calls.

WHAT THIS STUDY DOES NOT CLAIM

That convergence is an error. That a participant which changes position
performs worse. That disagreement implies independence. That effective
sample size measures knowledge, novelty or quality — it measures
observational redundancy with respect to the outcome whose dependence was
estimated, and nothing beyond that. That the observed dependence is
caused by conformity rather than by shared pre-training data: the
discount on N_eff holds under either mechanism, and this design does not
separate them.
